valueChange.when: The user chooses an enabled option other than the current value, or empties the input and leaves it while a value is set.
valueChange.payload: The value of the chosen option, or an empty value.

inputChange.when: The user edits the text of the input (typing, pasting, deleting) while the combobox is neither disabled nor readonly.

openChange.when: The list opens or closes because of the user: typing, an opening key, a press on the input or the indicator, an option chosen, Escape, focus leaving, a press outside.

rules: The panel holds the list of matching options. It is painted in surface with shadow, an edge of borderWidth in elevationColor and radius corners, with padding around the options. Its inline size is the combobox's inline size, wider when an option label needs it, up to the larger of the combobox's inline size and maxInlineSize. Its block size follows the options up to maxBlockSize and the room the viewport leaves; beyond it the list scrolls and keeps the highlighted option visible.

When no option matches, the panel shows empty instead of the list: emptyLabel in typographyEmpty and emptyColor with emptyPaddingInline and emptyPaddingBlock. It is not an option, is never highlighted, and is announced politely when it appears.
The panel is placed at offset below the combobox, aligned with its inline start; it flips above when the viewport lacks room below and shifts along the edge when it lacks room inline.

The panel inherits the brand, appearance and density of the combobox's surroundings and appears above the page without taking focus from the input. Where the platform has no top layer, it is stacked at layer.

It enters by fading in and moving enterDistance away from the combobox over motionDuration with easingEnter and leaves by fading out over motionDuration with easingExit; under reduced motion it only fades.
In forced-colors mode the panel keeps a visible edge in the system text color.

Each matching record of options renders one option, in order: label shows the record's label in typography (the Combobox's size), on one line, truncated with an ellipsis when the panel reaches its maximum inline size, and is the option's accessible name. The selected option shows check, a check mark of checkSize in checkColor at the inline end; other options keep its room so that labels do not move.
The option block size is the greater of minHeight and its content plus paddingBlock; paddingInline on both sides, gap between label and check, radius corners.

interaction hover is the highlighted option, reached by the pointer or the keyboard: at most one option is highlighted. interaction resolves in this order: disabled, selected-hover, selected, hover, default. Colors change over motionDuration with easingStandard; no transition under reduced motion.
An option whose record is disabled is listed, reached by the arrow keys and announced as unavailable, but cannot be chosen.

Consecutive matching records that carry the same non-empty group are gathered under a heading showing that group in typography and headingColor, with paddingInline and paddingBlock, aligned with the option labels. The heading is never highlighted or chosen; the group is exposed as a group named by its heading; a group without matching options is hidden.

contrast.note: Options are transparent by default and read on the panel.

rules: A combobox lets the user choose one value from a long list of options by typing to narrow it (a country, a person, a project). The value is always one of the options; free text is not a value. A short list without search is a Select; free text with suggestions is an InputText.

The combobox looks and sizes like an InputText of the same size: container, leading, input and indicator in that order. input holds the text on one line and scrolls inline to keep the caret visible; placeholder in placeholderColor shows while the text is empty. indicator is a downward chevron of iconSize in slotColor at the inline end; a press on it toggles the list and keeps focus in the input; it is not a separate stop in sequential focus. leading holds at most one decorative icon of iconSize in slotColor.

Horizontal spacing matches InputText: container has edgeInline inline padding, input has textInline on both inline sides, leading and indicator have slotInline on both inline sides. The container fills the inline size it is given; its block size is minHeight; the interaction target meets minTarget in the block dimension without enlarging the visible container. Paint container in surface with a border of borderWidth in border inside its boundary, corners of radius, and the text in content.

The accessible name is the label of the enclosing Field, otherwise the label prop; one of them is present and non-empty. label is not displayed; placeholder is never the accessible name. The input exposes that it controls a list box, whether it is expanded, and the highlighted option as its active option. Focus stays in the input while the list is open.
inputValue is the text of the input. When value is set, the text shows the selected option's label; choosing an option replaces the text with its label.

With filter contains, the list shows the options whose label contains the typed text, ignoring case and accents, in their original order; opening the list without typing shows every option. With filter none, the combobox shows options as given and the application updates them from inputChange (a search on a server).

Typing opens the list and highlights the first enabled matching option, so that Enter chooses it. A press on the input opens the list. Opening by Down Arrow highlights the selected option or the first enabled option; Up Arrow highlights the selected option or the last enabled option.

Keyboard in the open list: Down and Up Arrow move the highlight to the next or previous option without wrapping; Page Down and Page Up move it by the number of visible options; Enter chooses the highlighted enabled option; Alt with Down Arrow opens the list without moving the highlight. Home, End and the horizontal arrows keep moving the caret in the input. Disabled options are reached but not chosen.

Choosing an option sets value, emits valueChange when the value changed, replaces the text with its label and closes the list; focus stays in the input. Escape closes the list and restores the text to the selected option's label (empty when none).

When focus leaves the combobox or a press lands outside it, the list closes. If the text is empty, value becomes empty (valueChange when a value was set); otherwise the text is restored to the selected option's label and value does not change.
Pointer: moving over an option highlights it; a press on an enabled option chooses it.

Resolve condition in this order: disabled, readonly, invalid, focus, hover, default; focus is also an independent axis drawing a focus indicator of focusWidth in focusColor at focusOffset outside the container, with focusRadius corners, whatever the input modality.

A disabled combobox is removed from sequential focus and never opens. A readonly combobox stays focusable, its text can be selected and copied, but it never opens and its value cannot change; its value is submitted. Neither emits events.
Invalid and required are exposed to assistive technology; the visible error message and required marker belong to the enclosing Field, so an error is never conveyed by color alone.
Setting value, inputValue or open from the application updates the combobox without emitting events.
Color changes between conditions transition over motionDuration with easingStandard; the focus indicator appears without delay; no transition under reduced motion.

In forced-colors mode the container keeps a visible boundary in the system field colors, the placeholder stays distinguishable from a value, the disabled combobox uses the system disabled text color, the focus indicator stays visible and the highlighted option is shown in the system highlight colors.
